title: Adaptive kernel warmup orchestration for interleaved decode streams
creator: Elena Rivera
description: Problem: multi-stream decode on shared GPUs sees sporadic cudaGraph capture failures and non-deterministic kernel scheduling when streams hit cold code paths. These failures are amplified for mixed-quant and variable-seqlen workloads because kernel occupancy and chosen kernels vary at runtime. Goal: implement an orchestration layer that proactively warms and sequences small, deterministic 'micro-warmup' captures per stream and model variant to reduce capture jitter and improve replay correctness without significantly increasing tail latency or steady-state cost. This ticket implements the core orchestration, an occupancy fingerprinting profiler, and a conservative fallback policy for failed captures.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce capture-related replay errors on CI regression harness by >= 80% vs baseline (measured over 72-hour multi-model stress run)
P95 end-to-end latency regressed by <= 5% on representative chat workload after warmup orchestration enabled
No customer-facing errors introduced during canary rollout; canary run for 24h with traffic shaping completes without capture aborts
Automated integration test that simulates interleaved prefill+decode across 4 streams reproduces deterministic capture window; test added to nightly suite
tasks: Add lightweight occupancy-fingerprint profiler: sample kernel occupancy on first 5 requests per model-variant
Implement micro-warmup capture: record short capture segment (<=8 tokens) per stream during low-util windows
Orchestrator: slot-based priming that sequences warmups to avoid simultaneous heavy captures
Fallbacks: deterministic gate that reverts to non-cuda-graph path on repeated capture instability
Integration tests: CI harness + nightly stress test scenario + canary config
Benchmarks: run cost/latency delta matrix across int8/q4 and fp16 models
Docs: design note + rollout playbook + observability signals to add to Console
progress_updates: 2025-03-04: Spike completed for occupancy fingerprinting (prototype collects kernel launch metrics; utility validated on smallResNet-like model)
2025-03-06: Micro-warmup prototype implemented; initial tests show fewer intermittent capture timeouts but increased transient GPU occupancy during warmup slot
2025-03-09: Orchestrator scheduling added with slot randomized jitter to avoid thundering-warmup; reduced 99th percentile memory pressure in lab runs
2025-03-11: Integration test added to nightly; initial 24h run shows 4% P95 latency increase on synthetic chat load — investigating kernel selection path to re-tighten overheads
decisions: Use short deterministic capture segments ('micro-warmup' of 4-8 tokens) instead of full prefill replays to minimize cost and speed up priming
Fingerprinting collected on first few requests and cached per model/version; policy TTL 12 hours to handle shifts in traffic patterns
Slot-based orchestration chosen over opportunistic background warmup to ensure bounded concurrency of capture operations and predictable interference

On repeated capture instability (>=3 consecutive failed replays within 1 minute), automatically fall back to the non-cuda-graph kernel path for that stream until operator clears or new warmup succeeds
Do not enable micro-warmup by default for low-tier customers; rollout behind runtime-1.20 feature flag and dedicated config per deployment type (Hosted vs Dedicated)
blockers: Need updated NVidia driver on perf lab machines (driver 535+) to properly reproduce some mixed-quant kernel paths
Observability gap: Console currently shows only aggregate capture failure counts; need per-stream capture histograms to debug jitter sources
Small risk of increased GPU memory pressure during warmup slots on 24GB GPUs; capacity team verifying no OOMs under 3x canary scale
comments: Marco: initial perf numbers look promising but we should add an escape hatch flag to disable warmup per-host — done in PR 8167
Priya (PM): ensure canary includes a mix of short-chats and long-completions; short chats are most sensitive to added warmup latency
QA: reproduced a rare race where two streams attempt warmup simultaneously despite slotting; added extra jitter and a lightweight mutex per-GPU
Infra: schedule driver upgrades for perf lab week of 2025-03-17; dependent on change window approval
Follow-up: evaluate combining warmup fingerprint with model-quantization hints from Optimize to avoid warming heavy kernels unnecessarily
